definitions.explanation: A piece of furniture with drawers for storing clothes and other items. Traditional Japanese tansu are often made of paulownia wood.

examples.japanese: {洋服|ようふく}を{箪笥|たんす}にしまいました。
examples.english: I put the clothes away in the dresser.

examples.japanese: この{箪笥|たんす}は{祖母|そぼ}から{受|う}け{継|つ}いだものです。
examples.english: This chest of drawers was passed down from my grandmother.

examples.japanese: {桐|きり}の{箪笥|たんす}は{高級|こうきゅう}です。
{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しのとき、{重|おも}い{箪笥|たんす}を{二人|ふたり}で{運|はこ}んだ。
examples.english: When moving, we carried the heavy chest of drawers between two of us.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}は{季節|きせつ}ごとに{箪笥|たんす}の{中身|なかみ}を{入|い}れ{替|か}えて、{夏物|なつもの}と{冬物|ふゆもの}を{分|わ}けている。
examples.english: My mother swaps out the contents of the dresser each season, separating summer and winter clothes.

notes:
{箪笥|たんす} - the kanji is complex and often written in hiragana.

Traditional types:
- {桐|きり}{箪笥|たんす} (paulownia wood chest) - for kimono storage
- {階段|かいだん}{箪笥|たんす} (staircase tansu) - doubles as stairs
- {車|くるま}{箪笥|たんす} (wheeled tansu)
- {船|ふな}{箪笥|たんす} (ship tansu) - used on boats

{桐|きり} (paulownia) properties:
- Moisture resistant
- Protects from insects
- Lightweight yet durable
- Ideal for storing silk kimono

Expression:
- {箪笥|たんす}の{肥|こ}やし (lit. "fertilizer for the dresser") - clothes that are never worn

Modern equivalents: チェスト, ドレッサー
